topic: Sharp confidence length under heterogeneous rare network exposures. Partition n units into known unequal disjoint clique blocks B_l of sizes r_l and assign units independently Bernoulli(1/2). Outcomes are fixed in [-1/2,1/2], interference is confined to blocks, and each unit's target exposures are its whole block All Treat and All Control, each with probability q_l=2^(-r_l). For theta=n^(-1)sum_i[Y_i(a)-Y_i(b)], write w_l=r_l/n, S=sum_l w_l^2/q_l and M=max_l w_l/q_l. Construct a clipped block-specific HT interval with finite-sample length controlled by sqrt(S log(2/alpha))+M log(2/alpha), then prove that every uniformly randomization-valid measurable interval has worst-case expected length at least c min{1,sqrt(S log(1/alpha))) for 0<alpha<=1/4 whenever M sqrt(log(1/alpha))<=c0 sqrt(S). The lower bound must use a heterogeneous block-homogeneous weighted-erasure prior and cover randomized intervals. Recover the parent's equal-block theorem without its extreme-alpha artifact. Outside the no-dominant-block regime, derive a trimmed/water-filling modulus and the correct consistency boundary rather than claiming S alone is necessary. Implement the diagnostic for the R interference package's full-neighborhood exposure map. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolver derived the exact independent categorical block reduction, including mutually exclusive treatment/control reveals, variance at most S/2, increment bound M, and the clipped honest Bernstein interval. Normalized slopes a_l=w_l/(q_l sqrt(S)) satisfy sum q_l a_l^2=1 and sum w_l a_l=sqrt(S); the no-dominant-block condition keeps the proposed least-favourable Bernoulli prior interior. Exact two-block enumeration checked unbiasedness, variance, saturation, and all factors. Literature searches found no matching weighted all-measurable-interval theorem. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the weighted erasure posterior-spread lemma with universal constants at every conventional alpha, jointly controlling random weighted information, compact-prior boundaries, unrevealed target slope, conditional target fluctuation, and externally randomized intervals; then prove the water-filling characterization outside the Lindeberg regime. EARLY KILL TEST: Establish or refute that lemma for arrays with max_l a_l sqrt(log(1/alpha))->0. Any counterexample with vanishing dominance ratio stops the frontier; failure only of constants tightens c0. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_interference_heterogeneous_block_confidence_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish the sharp finite-sample confidence-length frontier for the all-treated versus all-control average effect under independent Bernoulli assignment on known unequal disjoint cliques, including every measurable externally randomized interval.

source_refs.claim: Exposure-probability-weighted estimators, randomization variance estimators, and local-dependence asymptotics are developed, but not finite-sample minimax expected-length bounds for heterogeneous rare exposures.
source_refs.author: Peter M. Aronow and Cyrus Samii

source_refs.claim: Full-neighborhood exposure under unit randomization may have exponentially small probability and exponentially large Horvitz–Thompson variance.
source_refs.author: Johan Ugander, Brian Karrer, Lars Backstrom, and Jon Kleinberg
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the 19th ACM SIGKDD Conference

source_refs.claim: Design-based minimax mean-squared-error bounds are derived from conflict graphs, but fixed-design confidence-set expected length and its alpha dependence are not characterized.
source_refs.author: Vardis Kandiros, Christopher Harshaw, and Fredrik Sävje

source_refs.excerpt: Strengthen thm:clique-block-minimax-comparison from equal-size cliques to known unequal partial-interference blocks
Unequal-block/conventional-alpha salvage requires genuinely new heterogeneous interval and weighted lower-bound research

open_problems.why_unsolved: The exposure-mapping literature controls Horvitz–Thompson estimators through marginal and joint exposure probabilities, while recent minimax work targets mean-squared error and often optimizes over both design and estimator. The closest prior CausalSmith theorem instead assumes a common clique size, a common reveal probability, and a binomial reveal count, and its posterior-spread argument reaches only an extreme-alpha regime. Unequal blocks produce an independent but nonidentical categorical weighted-erasure experiment: treatment and control reveals are mutually exclusive, random revealed information must be controlled, slopes proportional to w_l/q_l may hit the bounded-outcome boundary, conditional target fluctuation remains after conditioning, and auxiliary interval randomization must be incorporated into the converse.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-sample theorem proving coverage and length at most C min{1,sqrt(S log(2/alpha))+M log(2/alpha)} for an explicit clipped blockwise Horvitz–Thompson interval and a lower bound c min{1,sqrt(S log(1/alpha))} over all randomized measurable intervals whenever M sqrt(log(1/alpha))<=c0 sqrt(S).

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from network-experiment practice to a fundamental design-based precision limit and cleanly separates attainable procedures from converse bounds.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Interference makes estimand-relevant potential outcomes jointly unobservable -> existing procedures lack a fundamental precision benchmark -> design-based minimax analysis exposes the information bottleneck -> heterogeneous rare clique exposures require the corresponding confidence-length frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Use between-class moduli and testing reductions to lower-bound expected confidence-interval length uniformly over honest procedures, paired with modulus-driven interval constructions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is an honest expected-length problem for a bounded weighted linear functional, with a heterogeneous erasure experiment replacing Gaussian white noise.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct finite-sample bias-aware intervals from a modulus problem and compare them with unrestricted confidence procedures through efficiency bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides an econometric template for converting a deterministic modulus into both a valid interval and an alpha-specific lower benchmark.

method_exemplars.technique: Form exposure-specific Horvitz–Thompson contrasts from known exposure probabilities and control their design variance using joint exposure probabilities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: On disjoint cliques, the general exposure framework reduces exactly to independent block-level inverse-probability contributions.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the exact trimmed or water-filling confidence-length modulus and the necessary-and-sufficient consistency boundary for unequal clique arrays when one or more blocks violate the no-dominant-block condition.

source_refs.claim: Even structural restrictions permitting unbiased estimators need not produce decreasing variance under interference, so increasing n alone is not a consistency criterion.
source_refs.author: Guillaume W. Basse and Edoardo M. Airoldi

source_refs.claim: Exceptionally unlikely full-neighborhood exposures can make Horvitz–Thompson variance prohibitive, motivating design changes that mitigate unlucky vertices.
source_refs.author: Johan Ugander and Hao Yin

source_refs.claim: Removing difficult conflict-graph vertices can improve minimax MSE bounds, but the resulting subset problem is not a sharp, alpha-dependent fixed-design confidence modulus.
source_refs.author: Vardis Kandiros, Christopher Harshaw, and Fredrik Sävje

source_refs.excerpt: The result establishes the joint effective count n/(r2^r) only on the canonical clique-block class
only in the extreme regime alpha < exp(-1024) with Bq at least 4096 log(1/alpha)

open_problems.why_unsolved: A block with very large w_l/q_l can dominate the Bernstein increment, saturate the bounded parameter space, and leave a discrete target jump when its relevant outcome is unrevealed; the quadratic quantity S therefore ceases to describe recoverable information by itself. Existing network work diagnoses extreme exposure weights or removes difficult vertices for MSE, while the equal-block parent uses an uncapped common-slope prior. The missing step is an alpha-dependent optimization of capped block perturbations subject jointly to outcome bounds and erasure-information constraints, with an upper procedure that trims or saturates exactly the same coordinates.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit finite-dimensional convex program or closed-form water-filling modulus omega_alpha(w,q), matching upper and all-randomized-interval lower bounds of order min{1,omega_alpha(w,q)}, together with an if-and-only-if triangular-array condition for omega_alpha(w,q) to converge to zero.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative directly challenges the intuition that a large experiment automatically concentrates and motivates a structural consistency boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Large network experiments appear information-rich -> interference can prevent unbiased estimators from concentrating -> topology and observability, not n alone, govern precision -> unequal rare-exposure blocks require a dominance-aware consistency boundary

method_exemplars.technique: Trade bias against variance by excising difficult conflict-graph vertices and compare the resulting procedure with design-based minimax lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Coordinate capping in the clique sequence model is the tractable analogue of hard-vertex removal and should yield water-filling rather than a general subset search.

method_exemplars.technique: Express honest expected length through an ordered or between-class modulus and derive lower bounds from hard parameter pairs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired water-filling quantity is a confidence-interval modulus for a bounded weighted linear functional observed through heterogeneous channels.

method_exemplars.technique: Retain both variance and maximum-increment terms in Bernstein concentration for heterogeneous bounded summands.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The attainable upper bound must transition from a quadratic S regime to a dominant-coordinate regime, the two components separated by Bernstein's argument.

open_problems.open_problem: Extend the confidence-length characterization from disjoint cliques to a named general-graph family under vertex Bernoulli assignment and full-neighborhood exposure, using an overlap-aware conflict-graph or fractional-packing modulus that reduces to the weighted-clique formula.

source_refs.claim: Full-neighborhood exposure probabilities and Horvitz–Thompson variance under network randomization can depend exponentially on graph degree.
source_refs.author: Johan Ugander, Brian Karrer, Lars Backstrom, and Jon Kleinberg
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the 19th ACM SIGKDD Conference

source_refs.claim: Exposure conflict graphs encode estimand-relevant incompatibility and yield spectral variance bounds and asymptotically valid conservative intervals.
source_refs.author: Vardis Kandiros, Charilaos Pipis, Constantinos Daskalakis, and Christopher Harshaw

source_refs.claim: Design-based minimax MSE is governed by exposure conflict graphs, but only rate bounds rather than an alpha-dependent expected-confidence-length characterization are given.
source_refs.author: Vardis Kandiros, Christopher Harshaw, and Fredrik Sävje

source_refs.excerpt: Test whether the lower-bound construction extends from disjoint clique blocks to a broader nondegenerate family
Strengthen the lower-bound question beyond block compression by proving a graph-family frontier

open_problems.why_unsolved: The clique converse tensorizes independent categorical block reveals. On a general graph, closed neighborhoods overlap, so target-exposure indicators share treatment assignments and revealed outcomes may constrain several latent coordinates; the first proof step—the exact independent-erasure reduction—therefore fails. Conflict graphs capture pairwise incompatibility and existing minimax MSE rates, but do not supply the alpha-dependent posterior-spread inequality needed against all measurable confidence intervals. A resolution requires a fractional packing, hypergraph matching, or dependency-aware information inequality that controls simultaneously revealed target weight.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem for a concrete family such as high-girth d-regular graphs defining an overlap-aware modulus Omega_alpha(G), proving matching upper and randomized-all-interval lower bounds for the global treatment-effect confidence length, and showing that Omega_alpha(G) specializes to the heterogeneous-clique water-filling modulus.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames arbitrary-network difficulty through estimand-specific unobservability and a graph object, which is the required abstraction for the destination problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A causal contrast selects potential outcomes assignments may not jointly reveal -> incompatibilities form an exposure conflict graph -> graph geometry controls minimax estimation risk -> identify the alpha-sensitive graph modulus controlling honest interval length

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a modified Horvitz–Thompson estimator and conservative variance estimator from an exposure conflict graph, with risk controlled spectrally.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its conflict graph represents the overlapping exposure incompatibilities that replace independent clique erasures.

method_exemplars.technique: Use exposure conflict graphs for unrestricted minimax lower and upper risk bounds, combining spectral control with removal of difficult vertices.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired Omega_alpha(G) is the confidence-set and confidence-level-sensitive refinement of this graph-based minimax complexity.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive honest expected-length lower bounds from a modulus and testing affinity without restricting procedures to linear or deterministic intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This machinery can convert a graph-specific information modulus into a converse covering every measurable randomized interval.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct an observable variance-adaptive confidence interval for heterogeneous network-exposure contrasts that remains uniformly design-valid despite mutually exclusive target exposures and zero joint exposure probabilities.

source_refs.excerpt: The observable envelope replaces the schedule-specific design variance and can be conservative
replace the Wald-normal route with a finite-sample conservative inequality and a nontrivial minimality/sharpness

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parent upper bound substitutes a deterministic inverse-propensity envelope for schedule-specific variance and consequently cannot shorten on benign fixed outcome schedules. Ordinary empirical-Bernstein arguments require observable quadratic variation, but the all-treated and all-control outcomes of a block are mutually exclusive and relevant cross-products may have zero joint inclusion probability. The deterministic second-moment substitution must be replaced by an estimable conservative completion envelope or predictable variance process that controls the graph-colored exponential moment pathwise, rather than only in expectation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A computable convex-program or block-completion variance process producing a fractional-color empirical-Bernstein e-value and uniformly randomization-valid interval, together with an oracle inequality or minimality theorem showing strictly smaller expected length than the propensity-only S bound on a stated low-variance subclass.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames unobservable randomization variance as optimization over estimable conservative quadratic bounds, matching the central obstacle.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Design variance contains unobservable potential-outcome products -> interference creates zero joint exposure probabilities -> optimized estimable bounds reduce conservativeness -> convert the optimized bound into finite-sample exponential inference

method_exemplars.technique: Represent estimable conservative randomization-variance bounds as quadratic forms and optimize them through convex duality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the observable variance surrogate required when exact design variance is not estimable.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct variance-adaptive betting supermartingales for bounded observations and invert them into empirical-Bernstein confidence sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its proof is the closest template for turning an observable conservative variance process into finite-sample exponential coverage.

method_exemplars.technique: Aggregate exponential moments across dependent coordinates using exact-fold Hölder weights.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The adaptive construction must retain graph-dependent exponential-moment aggregation while replacing its fixed variance envelope.

open_problems.open_problem: Give an auditable finite-sample informativeness certificate for the R interference package's full-neighborhood exposure map that computes exact exposure probabilities and dependence components and attaches the proved heterogeneous-clique confidence frontier.

source_refs.claim: The review develops design-based spillover estimation and demonstrates the interference R package, but does not attach a sharp rare-exposure confidence-length diagnostic to an exposure map.
source_refs.author: Peter M. Aronow, Dean Eckles, Cyrus Samii, and Stephanie Zonszein

source_refs.claim: Under node-level independent randomization, full-neighborhood exposure probabilities are exponential in degree and can be extremely small.
source_refs.author: Johan Ugander and Hao Yin

source_refs.claim: Known marginal and joint exposure probabilities are the inputs to design-based Horvitz–Thompson estimation and randomization variance calculation.
source_refs.author: Peter M. Aronow and Cyrus Samii

open_problems.why_unsolved: The package operationalizes exposure mappings and Horvitz–Thompson analysis, while the methodological literature warns that full-neighborhood probabilities can be exponentially small; its software-facing outputs do not currently provide a theorem-backed decision rule for whether a requested contrast is informative at a chosen alpha. The first proof obligation is to show that the package's generated exposure labels and probabilities induce the categorical reveal experiment used by the finite-sample theory. For non-clique inputs, the diagnostic must compute dependence components rather than silently applying an independence formula.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A correctness theorem and reference implementation proving that the diagnostic returns exact q_l, S, and M on unequal disjoint cliques, emits the proved clipped Horvitz–Thompson interval, identifies the no-dominance or water-filling regime, and rejects or replaces the clique formula when overlapping neighborhoods invalidate it.

writing_exemplar.why: It connects exposure-mapping methodology directly to practitioner workflow and the interference package.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Spillovers require exposure-aware estimands -> known randomization enables inverse-probability analysis -> software makes those estimators usable -> rare full-neighborhood exposures require a certified informativeness diagnostic

method_exemplars.technique: Compute exact network-exposure probabilities under a specified randomization and use them as inverse weights in an unbiased Horvitz–Thompson estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The diagnostic must reproduce this probability-to-estimator pipeline before adding confidence-length and dominance certificates.

method_exemplars.technique: Use marginal and pairwise exposure probabilities to form design-unbiased contrasts and conservative randomization-variance estimators under general exposure mappings.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These are the canonical package quantities against which the exact clique-component diagnostic should be checked.

literature_map:
Aronow and Samii (2017, Annals of Applied Statistics) provide the canonical exposure-mapping, Horvitz–Thompson, randomization-variance, consistency, and local-dependence CLT framework.
Ugander, Karrer, Backstrom, and Kleinberg (2013, KDD) show that full-neighborhood exposure can have exponentially small probability and Horvitz–Thompson variance exponential in degree, while clustering can improve it dramatically.
Eckles, Karrer, and Ugander (2017, Journal of Causal Inference) emphasize the bias–variance tradeoff of graph-cluster randomization and leave robust network-dependent inference unresolved.
Basse and Airoldi (2018, Sociological Methodology) show that unbiasedness under interference need not imply concentration, undermining sample-size-only consistency intuition.
Leung (2022, Econometrica) obtains IPW consistency, asymptotic normality, and network-HAC inference under approximate neighborhood interference, but in a large-network asymptotic regime rather than finite-sample rare-exposure minimax inference.
Ugander and Yin (2023, Journal of Causal Inference) randomize graph clusterings to mitigate exceptionally small full-neighborhood exposure probabilities; their target remains variance or MSE rather than sharp confidence length.
Cortez-Rodriguez, Eichhorn, and Yu (2022, arXiv:2208.05553) derive variance, minimax-MSE, and asymptotic-normality results under low-order interaction restrictions, an alternative to exact rare full-neighborhood reveals.
Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw (2024, arXiv:2411.10908) introduce exposure conflict graphs, spectral Horvitz–Thompson variance bounds, conservative variance estimation, and asymptotic intervals.
Kandiros, Harshaw, and Sävje (2026, arXiv:2608.04909) develop unrestricted design-and-estimator minimax MSE theory and difficult-vertex trimming, but not fixed-design alpha-dependent expected confidence length.
Donoho (1994, Annals of Statistics) identifies moduli of continuity as the geometry governing minimax estimation and confidence procedures for linear functionals.
Cai and Low (2004, Annals of Statistics) give expected-length lower bounds for honest confidence intervals through between-class moduli and comparisons with unrestricted procedures.
Armstrong and Kolesár (2018, Econometrica) turn modulus calculations into finite-sample bias-aware econometric intervals and efficiency comparisons.
Harshaw, Middleton, and Sävje (arXiv:2112.01709) formulate minimally conservative randomization-variance estimation under interference as a convex optimization problem.
Aronow, Eckles, Samii, and Zonszein (2021, Advances in Experimental Political Science) connect exposure-based design inference to the interference R package, whose workflow lacks a sharp rare-exposure informativeness certificate.
The live tension is that network papers quantify rare-exposure variance or minimax MSE, while confidence-modulus papers control expected length in other experiments; the heterogeneous weighted-erasure bridge, randomized-interval converse, and water-filling frontier remain unoccupied.
